scenes.title: THE OBJECTS HAVE QUESTIONS
scenes.label: CASE NO. 001  /  HRIDYA JAIN
scenes.narration: A portfolio walked into an interrogation room. Four ordinary objects were the witnesses. Their testimony became The Objects Have Questions.

scenes.title: DETECTIVE MUG CLOCKS IN
scenes.label: ANIMATED REENACTMENT  /  NO MUGS WERE HARMED
scenes.bubble: I FOUND THE SUSPECT. IT'S A PORTFOLIO.
scenes.narration: Detective Mug arrived unpaid, overcaffeinated, and certain every object had a motive. First suspect: the portfolio itself.

scenes.title: THE NOTEBOOK TESTIFIES
scenes.label: EXHIBIT A  /  CREATIVE JUDGMENT
scenes.narration: The notebook saw Hridya reject idea after idea. The test was simple: could it be filmed, and would someone actually use it?

scenes.title: THE MICROPHONE OBJECTS
scenes.label: DRAMATIC REENACTMENT  /  STOCK FOOTAGE
scenes.card: I WAS READY FOR MY SOLO. THEN THE WORDS WENT STRAIGHT INTO THE BUILD.
scenes.narration: The microphone was ready for its big break. Wispr Flow got the speaking role.

scenes.title: THE FIRST BRIEF WAS SPOKEN
scenes.label: EXHIBIT B  /  WISPR FLOW
scenes.narration: Hridya dictated the first build brief with Wispr Flow into Emergent. Speaking let the whole idea come out in one natural pass, ready to build and revise.

scenes.title: THE WORDS BECAME A LIVE SITE
scenes.label: FROM SPOKEN BRIEF TO WORKING PORTFOLIO
scenes.quote: Build a cinematic comedy portfolio. Four everyday objects act as witnesses, each telling a funny but truthful story about the making of this project.
scenes.narration: That spoken brief was the start. The result is a live portfolio you can question, hear aloud, and explore, instead of another polished PDF.

scenes.title: NOW THE STUDIO IS OPEN
scenes.label: A TOOL ANYONE CAN USE
scenes.narration: Then the format became a public tool. Anyone can give an object a short story and an instruction, and share its case file with a QR code.

scenes.title: OBJECTION: IT IS USEFUL
scenes.label: DETECTIVE MUG  /  UNEXPECTED DISCOVERY
scenes.bubble: WAIT. THE QR CODE ACTUALLY DOES SOMETHING?
scenes.narration: The detective expected a punchline. Instead, the QR code opened a shareable case file. The joke had somehow become a useful label.

scenes.title: A MUG FILES A COMPLAINT
scenes.label: DRAMATIC REENACTMENT  /  STOCK FOOTAGE
scenes.card: THREE MEETINGS. ONE COLD COFFEE. ZERO RESPECT.
scenes.narration: Even the office mug wanted its day in court. Its testimony had one urgent demand: rinse me.

scenes.title: THE MUG HAS A STATEMENT
scenes.label: LIVE PREVIEW  /  NOT FILED
scenes.narration: This office mug survived three meetings and one cold coffee. Its practical advice? Rinse the evidence before it dries.

scenes.title: THE MUG SEEKS DAMAGES
scenes.label: ANIMATED REENACTMENT  /  SETTLEMENT PENDING
scenes.bubble: I DEMAND COMPENSATION. AND A SPONGE.
scenes.narration: The mug demanded emotional damages. We offered a QR tag and a rinse instruction. It accepted, pending review by its lawyer, the teapot.

scenes.title: MEET THE OBJECT PASSPORT
scenes.label: BORROW  /  RETURN  /  FIND
scenes.narration: The Object Passport adds a status, approved check ins, a private finder note when something goes missing, and a small printable QR tag.

scenes.title: ASK THE OBJECT
scenes.label: THE BORROWED UMBRELLA  /  FICTIONAL SAMPLE
scenes.narration: Visitors can ask what happened, how to use it, and where it belongs. The answer can be read aloud. Silly enough to watch, useful enough to keep.

scenes.title: THE EVIDENCE IS LIVE
scenes.label: WISPR FLOW HIRING CHALLENGE
scenes.narration: The evidence is live. Open a case file, then give an object on your desk its own. This is Hridya Jain's Wispr Flow hiring challenge build.
